neighbours.label: the closing piece of a split Turkish, Arabic or South Asian personal name ('Kem|al', 'Jam|il', 'Me|hta')
fire: Yesterday the minister Kemal spoke briefly to the press.
My cousin Jamil runs a small bakery near the station.
The paper by Rohan Mehta won the best student award.
In the novel, the young officer Kemal falls in love with Feride.
Our team leader Jamil booked the flights for everyone.
Dr. Priya Mehta will chair the session on Tuesday.
The poet Kemal read three new poems at the festival.
His brother Adil plays the oud in a wedding band.
quiet: Yesterday the minister Brown spoke briefly to the press.
My cousin James runs a small bakery near the station.
The paper by Rohan Smith won the best student award.
In the novel, the young officer Henry falls in love with Clara.
Our team leader Mark booked the flights for everyone.
Dr. Priya Jones will chair the session on Tuesday.
The poet Turner read three new poems at the festival.
His brother Tom plays the guitar in a wedding band.

predictions: Fires on the second piece of names like Kemal, Jamil, Mehta, Adil; quiet when the same sentence uses an English one-token name.
notes: Probe: 'Kemal Pasha' 0.75, 'Jamil' 0.50, 'Mehta' 0.41, 'Kamal' 0.29, but 'Bilal' 0.007 (so not every 'al'); 'nematocysts' 'oc' 0.55 shows some non-name pieces too. English-name controls 0.008-0.015.
